newsitem.title: USA: Prime Capital sees return to profitability.
newsitem.headline: Prime Capital sees return to profitability.

text.p: Prime Capital Corp said Tuesday it expects a return to profitability in the third quarter, and it expects to close several asset sale or securitization deals in the second half of this year.
The company reported a loss per share for the second quarter of $0.56 compared with a profit of $0.10.

Revenues were $1.7 million compared with $2.6 million. The company said its decline in revenue was mainly due to lower fee income, which consists of gains from the sale or securitization of financial contracts.
The $1.5 million provision for credit losses in the second quarter raised the company's loss reserves to $7.0 million.
Prime said it has allocated $4.6 million of these reserves to absorb the estimated losses from four customers whose finance transactions have a total value of $10.5 million.
"Three of the four situations involved fraud or material misrepresentation," alleged chairman and chief executive James Friedman about an issue announced June 16.
"However, we have made excellent progress toward resolving several of these issues and believe that our strategies to mitigate losses will be successful."
